From: Dana Whitfield

Subject: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Please send a short note (bullet points are fine) with the key drivers by Wednesday end of day. If you have a supporting schedule, attach it – I’ll pull what I need from that.

Thanks,
Dana

No need to walk through it Thursday morning unless something new surfaces; I have what I need. If you spot any other adjustments between now and then, flag them before EOD Wednesday.

Dana

[[ ## draft ## ]]
{"to": ["Dana Whitfield"], "cc": [], "subject": "Re: Margin clarification needed before Thursday", "summary": "Provides plain-terms Q3 vs Q2 gross margin explanation (41.2% vs 43.8%) with four drivers and offers to support Thursday if needed.", "body": "Dana,

Here's the quick read on the Q3 vs Q2 gross margin drop (41.2% vs 43.8%). Four drivers, in order of impact:

- Packaging invoice timing — roughly $180k of Q2 packaging costs hit Q3 instead, pulling margin down about 0.9 pts.
- Mix shift — Q3 had a higher share of lower-margin SKUs (the retail promo line), costing about 0.8 pts.
- Freight — spot rates on two west-coast lanes ran ~6% above Q2 average, about 0.5 pts.
- Pricing — one large account renewal at a 2% discount effective mid-quarter, about 0.4 pts.

Net effect: the 2.6 pt decline is almost entirely timing and mix, not a structural margin issue. Excluding the packaging timing, normalized margin lands around 42.1%.

I don't have a separate schedule beyond what Gabe attached — his breakdown covers the same items. If anything new surfaces before EOD Wednesday, I'll flag it.

Happy to join Thursday morning if you want backup during the discussion; otherwise you're set.

V", "attachment_refs": []}
